policy: Failing clauses `mcp-conformance test` reports on the wire that the agreement gate's own recordings cannot show, for the same subjects (the product leg of cargo xtask conformance; xtask/src/conformance/product.rs). The gate's server tap sits behind the everything server's Host/Origin check, and the reference host captures at rmcp's message seam, above HTTP; the recording proxy and the stdio wrapper see every exchange. Each entry names the leg (http | stdio | client), the requirement, optionally a substring of the trace's name, and why only the wire shows it. The leg fails on a finding not listed here and on an entry that no longer occurs. Every entry is triaged: its `why` opens with the class — `our-bug`, `suite-bug` or `spec-ambiguity`, the three the agreement ledgers use — and then says what the bytes show, which clause they meet, and what would close it. An entry leaves when that happens (a fix, a validator change, or a pin bump past an upstream fix); the leg fails on an entry that no longer occurs, so it cannot outlive its cause. Triaged 2026-10-13: the fifth entry, BASE-009 on the dns-rebinding-protection scenario's 403, was a validator false positive and left with its fix — the transport's security warning permits an Origin refusal's body to be a JSON-RPC error that has no id (`base.error-id-matches`, regression traces `corpus/good/http-origin-refused-without-id.jsonl` and its `2026-07-28` counterpart). The same recording showed the refusal body carrying `"id": null`, which the schema's `JSONRPCErrorResponse` does not admit; the everything server now leaves the member out. Triaged 2026-10-25: the third and fourth entries, LIFE-018 and TRAN-017 on the `sse-retry` scenario, left with the validator's negotiated-revision rule. That scenario's server answers the host's `initialize` with protocolVersion 2025-03-26, so the session ran under 2025-03-26, which no registry in this build describes; `mcp-conformance test` now lists the session as unjudged with that reason (`sessions.unjudged` in its JSON report) instead of judging it at the revision the client proposed (regression: `crates/mcp-trace-validator/tests/cli_negotiated.rs`).

findings.why: Class: suite-bug. The pinned suite 0.1.16's `initialize` client scenario serves the client from a test server that answers every message other than `initialize` and `tools/list` with HTTP 200 and `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":<the message's id>,"result":{}}` — so the host's `notifications/initialized`, which has no id, draws `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{}}` (recorded: seq 6-7 of the scenario's trace). A result with no id corresponds to no request; BASE-004: "Result responses MUST include the same ID as the request they correspond to." The validator is right and the host is not involved: it sent a conforming notification. Fixed upstream in the 0.2.0-alpha line — the test server bundled with 0.2.0-alpha.12 answers `notifications/initialized` with 202 and no body (read in its dist/index.js) — so this leaves when the stable pin moves to a release carrying that fix. The host's message-seam capture never sees the unsolicited body, which is why only the wire shows it.

Class: suite-bug. The same exchange: the suite 0.1.16 test server accepts the POSTed `notifications/initialized` with HTTP 200 and a body. TRAN-027: "If the server accepts the input, the server MUST return HTTP status code 202 Accepted with no body." The validator is right; fixed in the 0.2.0-alpha.12 test server as above, and it leaves with the same pin bump. HTTP status codes are invisible at the host's message seam.
